## Proof

Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable, infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with orthonormal basis $\{e_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift, $Se_n = e_{n+1}$.

Let $\mathcal{B}_2(\mathcal{H})$ denote the ideal of Hilbert-Schmidt operators. We claim
$$\operatorname{dist}(S, \mathcal{B}_2(\mathcal{H})) = 1.$$

### Upper bound: $\operatorname{dist}(S, \mathcal{B}_2) \le 1$

The zero operator is Hilbert-Schmidt, so
$$\operatorname{dist}(S, \mathcal{B}_2) \le \|S - 0\| = \|S\|.$$
Since $S$ is an isometry ($\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for all $x$), $\|S\| = 1$. Hence $\operatorname{dist}(S, \mathcal{B}_2) \le 1$.

### Lower bound: $\operatorname{dist}(S, \mathcal{B}_2) \ge 1$

Every Hilbert-Schmidt operator is compact, so $\mathcal{B}_2(\mathcal{H}) \subseteq \mathcal{K}(\mathcal{H})$, the ideal of compact operators. Therefore
$$\operatorname{dist}(S, \mathcal{B}_2) \ge \operatorname{dist}(S, \mathcal{K}(\mathcal{H})) = \|S\|_e,$$
where $\|S\|_e$ is the **essential norm** (the norm of the image of $S$ in the Calkin algebra $\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{H}) = \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})/\mathcal{K}(\mathcal{H})$).

It remains to compute $\|S\|_e$. We have
$$S^*S = I, \qquad SS^* = I - P_0,$$
where $P_0$ is the rank-one projection onto $\operatorname{span}\{e_0\}$. Since $P_0$ is compact, in the Calkin algebra (with quotient map $\pi$):
$$\pi(S)^*\pi(S) = \pi(I), \qquad \pi(S)\pi(S)^* = \pi(I) - \pi(P_0) = \pi(I).$$
Thus $\pi(S)$ is **unitary** in the Calkin algebra. A unitary element has norm $1$, so
$$\|S\|_e = \|\pi(S)\| = 1.$$

Combining,
$$\operatorname{dist}(S, \mathcal{B}_2(\mathcal{H})) \ge \|S\|_e = 1.$$

### Conclusion

$$\operatorname{dist}(S, \mathcal{B}_2(\mathcal{H})) = 1.$$

The key structural reason: the unilateral shift is essentially unitary (it becomes unitary modulo compact operators), so its essential norm is $1$. Since Hilbert-Schmidt operators lie inside the compact operators, no Hilbert-Schmidt perturbation can reduce the norm below the essential norm, and the zero operator (which is Hilbert-Schmidt) attains the upper bound $\|S\| = 1$.
